messages:
Alex: morning passback — quick summary of overnight. we had repeated 503s in dedicated-pool-2 between 03:12–04:05 UTC. oncall-bot paged ~6x for latency/503s. key symptoms: KV cache evictions + redis backlog -> streamer queue growth.
Maria: saw elevated p95 and a lot of `kv_eviction` logs. Looks like autoscaler launched and then cycled nodes rapidly.
Sam: yep, autoscaler thrash. traced to new autoscale-policy v2 that had aggressive downscale window. nodes were removed while KV still warming -> cache-miss storms.
Ingrid: customer impact: 3 paying customers saw degraded responses (~30–60s) and some 503s. no billing-impact alert yet. support ticket #1382 opened.
Alex: mitigation done overnight:
- rolled back autoscale-policy to v1
- pinned warmup delay to 180s
- routed 10% traffic to fallback region eu-west-1
- temporarily enabled model-fallback to smaller quantized variant
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-8472. Severity: SEV2. Links: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-8472
Sam: commands I ran:
```
# increase KV retention threshold
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/kv-cache CACHE_RETENTION=600
# pin autoscaler
kubectl -n infra patch hpa autoscaler --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3}}'
```
Maria: logs snippet from the time:
```
[03:17:12] kv_eviction: evicted 240 keys, tenant=acme
[03:17:13] stream_queue: backlog=420, consumer_lag=3.1s
[03:18:05] http 503 GET /v1/generate tenant=acme
```
Ingrid: current status (as of last check): dedicated-pool-2 healthy, 503s down to baseline. fallback routing still at 10%. latency p95 back to 220ms from 1.8s. support ticket updated.
Alex: outstanding risks:
- if autoscale policy still misbehaves under sudden load spike we could see relapse
- warming period might still be too short for large seqlen workloads
Sam: next immediate actions before handoff:
- monitor kv_eviction rate for 2 more hours
- keep fallback routing at 10% until we confirm stability
- create postmortem skeleton (I can start)
Maria: I've updated the runbook pointers in the incident:
https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-warmup
https://redwood.internal/runbooks/autoscale-policy-debug
Alex: who is primary for next shift? Ingrid, are you ok taking primary for the next 6 hours?
Ingrid: I can take primary for 06:00–12:00 UTC. Sam will be secondary.
Sam: I'll be on standby, can jump on pager if pages spike.
Alex: handoff checklist:
- primary: review self-healing metrics (kv_eviction, stream_backlog, p95)
- ensure fallback routing toggle is accessible (ops console)
- assign postmortem owner (Sam volunteered)
- update customers in support tickets with latest ETA
Ingrid: noted. I'll run the daily health script at shift start:
```
./scripts/daily_health_check --pools dedicated-pool-2 --metrics kv_eviction,stream_backlog,p95
```
Alex: runbook excerpts:
- if kv_eviction > 100/min for >5min -> scale retention + hold downscale
- if stream_backlog > 300 -> enable fallback region
- if p95 > 1s -> open SEV2 and notify support
Maria: minor housekeeping: deploy-bot executed a non-critical infra rollout at 02:50 which we think contributed to jitter. deploy-bot: can you confirm the rollout config ID?
deploy-bot: rollout #infra-2026-07 completed at 02:49 UTC. config delta: autoscale-policy=v2 (beta)->v1 (stable) rollback already applied.
Alex: docs & follow-ups:
- Sam to draft postmortem and link runbook gaps (due EOD)
- Maria to add a warmup-sla note to the model onboarding doc
- Ingrid to maintain primary watch for 6 hours
Any other blockers?
Sam: none from me. I'll start the postmortem draft now.
Ingrid: I'll post an update + attach graphs at 07:30 UTC.
Alex: thanks team. passing primary to Ingrid. secondary Sam. contact channel for rapid paging: #eng-oncall. :thumbsup:
oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: primary=Ingrid secondary=Sam shift=06:00-12:00 UTC.
